rows.selection_reason: The existing evidence is empty, so the first experiment should explore a balanced multimodal configuration. This experiment tests a transformer-based aggregation with weighted fusion, using standard encoders (resnet50 for images, pca_n2000 for RNA) to establish a baseline for multimodal performance. It clarifies the effectiveness of transformer aggregation and weighted fusion in a multiprofile setting, which are key design choices with potential high impact.

The existing evidence shows config_001 (multimodal, pca_n2000+resnet50, transformer+weighted) achieves 0.5729 accuracy. This experiment tests replacing the RNA encoder with scgpt and image encoder with imagenet_vit_l while retaining the successful aggregation/fusion strategy. It clarifies whether advanced encoders (scgpt, vit_l) can improve performance without changing the proven transformer+weighted framework, balancing exploration of key components with exploitation of prior success.

The existing evidence shows config_001 (multimodal, multiprofile, pca_n2000, resnet50, transformer, weighted) achieves the highest accuracy so far (0.5729). This experiment tests replacing the image encoder with imagenet_vit_l while keeping other components identical, to evaluate if a more powerful image encoder could improve accuracy. This balances exploitation (building on the current best) and exploration (testing a key component change).

Existing evidence shows config_047 (pca_n2000 + imagenet_vit_l with transformer aggregation and weighted fusion) achieves the highest accuracy so far (0.5856). This experiment tests whether switching to avgpool aggregation and concat fusion (config_021) could improve performance, clarifying if the current aggregation/fusion choices are optimal. It balances exploitation of the top-performing RNA/image encoder pair with exploration of alternative aggregation methods, which are critical for multimodal integration.

The existing evidence shows config_021 (avgpool+concat) achieves the highest accuracy so far (0.6287). This experiment tests whether changing fusion from concat to weighted while keeping RNA/image encoders and aggregation the same could improve performance. It clarifies if fusion type is a critical factor, balancing exploitation of current best practices with exploration of alternative components.

Existing evidence shows that config_002 (pca_n2000 RNA, imagenet_vit_l image, avgpool, weighted) achieves the highest accuracy so far (0.6352). This experiment tests replacing the image encoder with resnet50 while keeping other components the same, to determine if the image encoder choice is critical. It directly addresses uncertainty about whether imagenet_vit_l or resnet50 is better for this task, leveraging the current top-performing configuration as a baseline.

The existing evidence shows that configurations using pca_n2000 RNA and resnet50 image encoders (e.g., config_041) achieve high accuracy (0.638999). This experiment tests transformer aggregation and concat fusion with the same RNA/image encoders, exploring whether changing aggregation/fusion methods could further improve performance. It balances exploitation of the current top-performing RNA/image encoder pair with exploration of alternative aggregation/fusion strategies.

The existing evidence shows that configurations using avgpool aggregation and weighted fusion (e.g., config_041 with 0.6389 accuracy) perform best. This experiment tests replacing the RNA encoder (pca_n2000 → scvi_n200) while keeping resnet50 image encoder, avgpool aggregation, and weighted fusion, which are key components of the current top performer. This clarifies whether the RNA encoder choice significantly impacts performance, leveraging the strong evidence from existing configurations to explore a critical design parameter.

The existing evidence shows config_049 (scvi_n200, resnet50, avgpool, weighted) achieves the highest accuracy so far (0.6776). This experiment tests using transformer aggregation instead of avgpool with the same RNA/image encoders and weighted fusion, which could potentially improve performance by capturing more complex interactions. It directly builds on the current best configuration, balancing exploitation of proven components with exploration of aggregation method variation.

Existing evidence shows config_024 (transformer aggregation, weighted fusion) achieves the highest accuracy (0.713). This experiment tests transformer aggregation with concat fusion, which could clarify if fusion method impacts performance. It's the best use of the last budget slot to explore a critical design choice (fusion type) that might improve upon the current best.
